convergence.seed_protocol: SeedSequence(root).spawn(budgets * 2 * n_seeds); budget/method/replicate order; uint64 child seeds
convergence.stream_design: Fresh independent pseudorandom streams for each budget, method, and replicate; no shared draws
convergence.interval_method: estimate +/- 1.96 * sample standard error; paired means for antithetic
convergence.cost_model: Equal discounted-payoff evaluations: N plain normals versus N/2 antithetic normals and N/2 independent pairs; excludes runtime and RNG costs

portfolio_calibration.data_source: Generated synthetic price CSV; no market observations
limitations: Historical close-to-close covariance is used as a constant scenario and pricing volatility proxy; it is not an implied volatility surface.
The drift remains the fixed 3% rate, not an estimated physical expected return. These are model scenarios, not validated real-world tail probabilities.
252 equal trading steps per year are assumed; supply consecutive synchronized adjusted daily closes. No holiday, split or dividend adjustment is inferred.
Gaussian GBM discards skewness, heavy tails and volatility clustering, even when present in the input CSV. Calibration does not validate this model.
Twelve scramble changes measure numerical variability only; parameter uncertainty and out-of-sample accuracy are unmeasured.

portfolio_model_risk.data_source: Generated synthetic price CSV; no market observations
portfolio_model_risk.method: plain Monte Carlo with common normal draws across models

model_specification.name: Two-state common horizon variance mixture
model_specification.terminal_formula: S_h = S_0 exp((r - V sigma^2/2) h + sigma sqrt(h V) L Z)
model_specification.pricing_rule: Fixed fitted-volatility Black-Scholes for both initial and future book values

portfolio_model_risk.seed_protocol: Normal draws: default_rng(seed).standard_normal((paths, 4)); independent regime uniforms: default_rng(SeedSequence(seed, spawn_key=(3103,))).random(paths). Same normals across models; one V shared by all assets in a path.

cost.scope: Two models at one displayed seed plus twelve paired seeds; excludes calibration, random generation, runtime and quantum oracle costs

limitations: The variance states and 10% probability are specified sensitivity assumptions, not fitted or selected by held-out performance. Input covariance alone does not identify tail shape.

E[V]=1 matches innovation covariance; random conditional drift adds a small term to log-return covariance. Conditional drift preserves expected terminal spots. This is a finite Gaussian mixture, not a power-law tail model.
One common variance state persists over the entire horizon; there is no time evolution, transition estimation, leverage effect or volatility-clustering validation.
Black-Scholes repricing volatility stays fixed in both models, isolating scenario sensitivity; this is not consistent mixture-model option pricing or a fitted volatility surface.

Twelve paired seed differences describe numerical variability only, not parameter uncertainty, tail coverage, market accuracy or out-of-sample validation. The 3% drift is illustrative, not fitted physical drift.
Synthetic bundled prices; no real-world accuracy or quantum advantage is established. Portfolio tail risk remains separate from the bounded quantum oracle.

bounded_exposure.data_source: Generated synthetic price CSV; no market observations
bounded_exposure.method: scrambled Sobol normals; mixture uses independent pseudorandom regimes
bounded_exposure.quantity: Mean positive undiscounted future net book value, USD, at 21/252 years; not PFE, VaR or CVA
bounded_exposure.error_identity: estimate - empirical mean = truncation + grid + amplitude-estimation error; add empirical mean - independent reference for reference difference
bounded_exposure.measurement_protocol: Existing maximum-likelihood estimator: powers 0,1,2,4,8; 256 shots each; measurement seed equals display seed. Direct baselines use SeedSequence(seed, spawn_key=(404,)), Bernoulli then grid draws. The amplitude-estimation error includes finite shots and the existing 32769-point theta likelihood search; it is signed realized error, not an RMSE.

costs.description: Precompute four option values per path, then O(paths) histogram for each cap/grid. Dense Householder preparation and Grover matrices; query counts exclude classical preprocessing, gates, inference, memory and runtime. Classical exact histogram expectation is already available; equal calls/draws do not imply equal runtime.

limitations: The oracle represents a finite empirical exposure law, not the continuous scenario distribution. Its probabilities require classical book revaluation first; no efficient coherent pricing circuit is supplied.
Capping and floor rounding bias the mean down. Measured tail excess is empirical, not a bound on the population tail. Grid rounding is bounded by cap/(levels-1) for any exposure distribution.
The independent high-budget mean is also numerical. Twelve scrambles measure scenario variability, not parameter or model uncertainty; the mixture regimes are pseudorandom.

The likelihood interval is conditional on the encoded grid only; it excludes cap, grid and scenario errors and has no tested coverage guarantee here. One measurement trial per model cannot establish estimator superiority.
Synthetic inputs, historical-volatility pricing proxy and specified mixture assumptions do not establish market accuracy. No quantum advantage, default exposure or hardware performance is claimed.

amplitude_coverage.data_source: Generated synthetic price CSV; no market observations
amplitude_coverage.seed_protocol: SeedSequence(root).spawn(targets * trials * 2), target/trial/method order, uint64 child seeds; separate amplitude and classical streams. Legacy and endpoint-inclusive inference share counts.
amplitude_coverage.interval_method: Legacy 32769-point open theta mesh; endpoint-inclusive adds exact theta=0,pi/2. Same fixed log-likelihood drop 1.920729. Report hull and direct likelihood-set membership separately. Classical baseline: exact equal-tailed Clopper-Pearson, 8960 power-zero shots.
amplitude_coverage.cost_model: Fixed powers 0,1,2,4,8 with 256 shots each: 1280 shots, 8960 preparation/inverse calls. Classical baseline uses 8960 independent power-zero preparations. Logical query equality excludes preprocessing, inference, gates, noise and runtime.
limitations: Conditional on fixed empirical capped/grid exposure, not coverage of uncapped population exposure, PFE or VaR. No new scenario paths or parameter fits per measurement trial.

Asymptotic likelihood cutoff has no finite-sample coverage guarantee, especially at boundaries. Adding endpoints repairs support exclusion but does not calibrate coverage. The original estimator remains unchanged.
Finite mesh can miss modes or set edges; hull can bridge excluded gaps. Direct truth membership uses the mesh maximum and is also numerical. No interpolated edges or mesh-convergence guarantee.
Coverage uncertainty intervals describe finite independent pseudorandom trials per target, with no multiple-comparison correction. Bias and RMSE are also finite-trial estimates.

Synthetic bundled data and ideal noiseless binomial measurements. Dense oracle and exact histogram mean already require classical answer-bearing preprocessing; no hardware or quantum advantage follows.

provenance.data: Call benchmark: synthetic risk-neutral GBM; portfolio comparison records its own dated CSV provenance

limitations: Normal approximation confidence intervals, not finite-sample guarantees.
Coverage and RMSE have sampling uncertainty across a finite set of seeds; no calibration or monotonic convergence guarantee.
One synthetic option parameter setting; equal payoff counts do not establish a runtime speedup.
The bounded exposure oracle estimates an empirical capped/grid mean, not portfolio tail risk; its classical preprocessing already determines the exact grid expectation.
CSV calibration uses constant historical covariance with risk-neutral drift; it does not establish real-world tail accuracy.
